rv.q: I felt braced, even a little giddy — like Anna standing on the deck of Chris's barge, her shoulders dropping in the mists of Provincetown harbor.

Even as the script veers overly melodramatic or just plain creaky, its unaddressed issues roiling beneath the surface, director Thomas Kail furnishes ample aesthetic compensation – enough to keep a contemporary audience happily occupied.
In 2025, a woman conforming to societal expectations and suffering shame for sex work feels discouraging.
Instead, it feels as unmoored as one of its barges, and overall a little lost in the muffling mists of that old devil sea.
It's a perfectly respectable production, but I'm not convinced the play has much to offer.
